candidates.name: V7 N/P rebalance 1.16 (neg 100um, pos 66um)
candidates.role: rebalance N/P from baseline 0.86 (anode-limited, anode saturates at every charge end) to ~1.16 while keeping cell capacity ~5 Ah: anode stays less lithiated at charge end, reducing SEI growth per cycle and the 4C plating dip

candidates.name: V8 N/P rebalance 1.36 (neg 110um, pos 62um)
candidates.role: stronger rebalance (~1.36) with capacity ~4.7 Ah (positive-limited); 4C test at 20 A then runs at ~4.25C actual - stricter test, honest

llm_reason: R3 diagnosis: (1) V6 (anode r3um + por 0.40) is within 2 mV of no-plating (-0.0017 V) - anode-side polarization levers nearly suffice; (2) C1 (k_SEI x0.4) only moves SEI@500 by -4.2% - the ec-reaction-limited model is in the grown-SEI regime where k largely drops out (j_sei = F*c0*k_exp/(1+L*k_exp/D_ec) -> F*c0*D_ec/L), so the coating bridge alone cannot reach 550 nm; (3) V2's +15.4% SEI@100 exactly matches its +16% cycle time - SEI thickness tracks time-at-low-anode-potential. Baseline is anode-limited (pos capacity ~5.74 Ah vs neg ~4.95 Ah -> N/P~0.86): the anode saturates every charge end (delta_phi -> ~0.06 V vs U_SEI 0.4 V), maximizing the exp(-alpha*F*eta/RT)-amplified growth during each cycle. V7/V8 rebalance N/P toward 1.15-1.35 WITHOUT changing cell capacity (thinner cathode compensates thicker anode, cycle time ~constant), so the anode charge-end potential stays higher: less SEI per cycle AND less 4C plating at the cutoff (both binding constraints attacked by one mechanism). NMC is the heavy layer, so ED rises. Parameter sources: design choices from baseline Chen2020 values (architecture freedom).
